{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Malcolm Roy Beasley''' (born January 4, 1940, in San Francisco)<ref name=AAAS /> is an American physicist. He is professor emeritus of applied physics at [[Stanford University]].  He is known for his research related to [[superconductivity]].<ref name=NAS />

==Early life and education==
Beasley was born at [[Stanford hospital]], moving to [[Hawaii]] during [[World War II]] with his parents, who were social scientists.<ref name="stanford98">{{cite news |last1=Manuel |first1=Diane |title=Malcolm Beasley new H&S dean |url=https://news.stanford.edu/news/1998/october7/beasley107.html |work=Stanford Report |date=October 7, 1998}}</ref> He was a high school and college [[basketball]] player, earning All-Metropolitan honors at [[Montgomery Blair High School]] in [[Silver Spring, Maryland]],<ref>{{cite news |title=1957 Schoolboy All-Star Teams |work=The Washington Post |date=March 3, 1957 |page=C3 |quote=Malcolm (Mac) Beasley, Montgomery Blair, Forward, All-Metropolitan First Team}}</ref> and playing for the [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell Big Red]] in 1958-59.<ref>{{cite web |title=1958-59 Men's Basketball Roster |url=https://cornellbigred.com/roster.aspx?roster=985&path=mbball |website=Cornell University Athletics |accessdate=31 May 2019}}</ref>

At [[Cornell University]], Beasley earned his [[bachelor's degree]] in engineering physics in 1962 and his [[Ph.D.]] in 1967.<ref name="AIP">{{cite web |title=Malcolm R. Beasley |url=https://www.aip.org/aip/governing-board/malcolm-r-beasley |website=American Institute of Physics |date=February 7, 2014}}</ref> His Ph.D. thesis ''Flux creep in hard superconductors''<ref>{{cite web|author=Beasley, M. R.|title=Thesis/Dissertation: ''Flux creep in hard superconductors''. Report No. 921|website=Office of Scientific and Technical Information, U.S. Dept. of Energy, osti.gov|url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/4496390|date=January 1, 1968}}</ref> was supervised by [[Watt W. Webb]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Malcolm Roy Beasley|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=168443}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Beasley joined the faculty of Harvard University in 1968 where he remained until accepting a position at Stanford in 1974.<ref name=APS>{{cite web|title=Malcolm Beasley, Stanford University: Candidate for Vice President|url=http://www.aps.org/about/governance/election/beasley.cfm|work=American Physical Society|accessdate=May 29, 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713024337/http://aps.org/about/governance/election/beasley.cfm|archivedate=July 13, 2011}}</ref> He was recruited to Stanford by [[Theodore Geballe]], and after [[Aharon Kapitulnik]] joined the applied physics department, the three Stanford superconductivity researchers became known as the "KGB Group."<ref name="stanford98"/>

In 1991, Beasley was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter B|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|accessdate=May 29, 2011}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 1993.<ref name=NAS>{{cite web|title=Beasley, Malcolm R.|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/1394540066?pg=vprof&mbr=1001687|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324090933/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/1394540066?pg=vprof&mbr=1001687|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 24, 2012|work=National Academy of Sciences|accessdate=May 29, 2011}}</ref>

In 1998, Beasley was named dean of the [[Stanford University School of Humanities and Sciences|School of Humanities and Sciences]] at Stanford.<ref name="stanford98"/>

In 2002, Beasley served as chairman of the [[Jan Hendrik Schön]] commission, which determined that Schön fabricated much of his published research.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chang |first1=Kenneth |title=Panel Says Bell Labs Scientist Faked Discoveries in Physics |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/09/26/us/panel-says-bell-labs-scientist-faked-discoveries-in-physics.html |work=The New York Times |date=September 26, 2002}}</ref>

In 2011, Beasley was elected to the Presidential line of the [[American Physical Society]], becoming APS President in 2014.<ref>{{cite news |title=Members Elect Beasley to the APS Presidential Line |url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201108/beasley.cfm |work=APS News |issue=August/September 2011 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>
